pairs.why: The real jelly is turned a little off-axis with a diagonal tentacle flow, and A's tilted bell and swept tentacles read closer to that than B's near-symmetric front-on pose, though both sit on a flat radial-ray backdrop.
The real calculator is rotated and tipped to show its top face and side thickness, and B's stronger rotation and tilt come closer to that than A's nearly front-on slab.
Both show the same mild high-front camera, and each has a plain wavy backdrop and a flat ground band. Neither is clearly nearer to the real card's ground and horizon placement.
B's milder perspective and shallower base plate sit closer to the real card's near-side-profile duck on a diamond plate, while A's exaggerated high angle makes the spring and plate look wide-angle.
The real clock is a wall-mounted disc with a soft diagonal shadow on a striped wall, and A keeps that wall reading. B adds a floor line and ground shadow that give it a different ground plane.
A's large foreground table with stools in front and a readable tilted top matches the real card's near, medium-high camera and layered depth. B's table is small and distant with a more top-down top.
A has the wall-mounted clock with a slight off-axis oval and a soft cast shadow like the real card, whereas B places it on a floor line, which makes the spatial reading wrong.
Both use the same mild front camera and a flat ground band under a simple wavy background, with no clear difference in view or depth against the real card.
